newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber buoyed by buying on Japan's rise.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber buoyed by buying on Japan's rise.

text.p: The Singapore rubber market was boosted at the close on Monday by active shortcovering for RSS3 grade rubber following gains in Tokyo, dealers said.

The Tokyo market got a boost from the rise of the U.S. dollar against the yen, prompting investors to cover their shorts. "I think some Japanese houses probably bought RSS3 rubber. There were also other players engaged in fairly active buying this afternoon," a dealer said.
Trading for other rubber grades remained thin, with sentiment weighed by concerns over the region's currency markets and news Bangkok defaulted on taking delivery of rubber.
Dealers said Michelin and Bridgestone were said to have made inquiries in the market to buy some rubber, but no deals were apparently concluded by the two companies.

"Michelin wanted to buy and Bridgestone asked for some offers. I'm not sure if they managed to clinch a deal," one dealer said. Michelin, which has been engaged in routine buying for its monthly programme, was looking for RSS3 rubber.
At 0945 GMT, September RSS3 was seen at 95.25 U.S. cents a kg from 94.75 cents. September RSS1 was seen unchanged at 139.75 Singapore cents (95 U.S. cents) a kg from 139.25 cents.
